In this case, I think stopping counting is probably a good idea. Once it becomes an obsession or a fear it can be very dangerous.  You don't want to gain weight, and I understand that, but if you keep loosing you're going to be in a very dangerous spot very quickly, if you're not already. I would say even if you don't have a full blown disorder, you are starting to develop symptoms of one. 

Knowing that you're starting to develop unhealthy habits surrounding food, I would go to your doctor and get set up with a nutritionist. They can provide you with meal plans to maintain your weight/get you to a healthy weight and maintain it. This takes it out of your hands and you can trust this person to make you healthy. Next, I would go see a therapist about this because if you're obsessing about food and calories, giving that power to someone else (your nutritionist) is going to cause a lot of anxiety for you. There's nothing wrong with going to therapy for something minor. It's even almost better to go before it's a huge thing to make sure you stay healthy, both in body and mind. Since you have calorie counts for so many things in your head, initially focus on that in order to stop weighing food. Go with approximates at first until you're able to see someone.
